newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish truckers end four-day blockade -- agency.
newsitem.headline: Danish truckers end four-day blockade -- agency.

text.p: Danish truckers voted on Thursday to end immediately a four-day blockade of seaports and the land border with Germany that has disrupted domestic and export trade, Danish news agency Ritzau said.

It added that a meeting of around 2,000 drivers at protest headquarters at the Padborg border crossing voted overwhelmingly to end their protest over subsistence allowances and began moving towards their vehicles shortly after 2000 GMT.
"Let's drive -- now!" drivers shouted, after protest leaders, a lawyer and sympathisers urged them to end the blockade before public opinion turned irrevocably against them, Ritzau said.
The blockade, of goods traffic only, was not related to nationwide protests by French truckers.
Police said that it would probably take most of the night before an estimated 2,000 lorries at Padborg could be moved and traffic restored to normal.

"We are regulating traffic to prevent chaos and it will, take time before conditions are normal again. Trucks should not count on getting in or out of the country before dawn," a duty officer at Padborg police told Ritzau.

The Danish protest stopped most movement of goods between Denmark, Britain, Germany, Norway and Sweden and paralysed shipments from the Jutland peninsula, where most food is produced, to the capital, Copenhagen, on the island of Zealand.
It also sent shockwaves abroad, combining with the French action to threaten production at Sweden's Volvo and Saab vehicle manufacturers.

Drivers had earlier said that a government offer to drop its planned abolition of a 150 Danish crown ($25.50) daily allowance for foreign trips and instead raise it to 250 crowns was inadequate and they demanded 500 crowns.
It was not clear if, or how, they intended to continue their campaign. ($1=5.884 Danish Crown)
